11.title: Units & Measurements
11.summary: Master dimensional formulas of constants (G, h, η, permeability), principle of homogeneity, and propagation of percentage errors: ΔZ/Z = a(ΔA/A) + b(ΔB/B).

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula for the Universal Gravitational Constant (G)?
questions.explanation: From F = G(m₁m₂)/r², G = F·r²/(m₁m₂). Substituting dimensions: [M L T⁻²][L²] / [M²] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].

11.title: Laws of Motion
11.summary: High yield: Free Body Diagrams (FBD), impulse J = Δp = F·Δt, apparent weight in elevators, and limiting static friction f_max = μ_s · N.

questions.question: A 2kg block rests on a rough floor (μs = 0.4). If a 5N force is applied horizontally, static friction force is:
questions.explanation: Limiting friction f_max = μs·m·g = 0.4 × 2 × 9.8 = 7.84 N. Because applied force (5N) is less than limiting friction, static friction adjusts to equal 5 N.

12.title: Electric Charges and Fields
12.summary: Crucial concepts: Coulomb's Law in vector form, torque on dipole (τ = p × E), potential energy (U = -p · E), and Gauss's Law for infinite line and plane sheet.

questions.question: An electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform field E. The torque is maximum when the angle between p and E is:
questions.explanation: Torque is τ = pE sin(θ). The sine function attains its maximum value of 1 when θ = 90°.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric flux (Φ)?
questions.explanation: Flux Φ = E · A = (Force / Charge) × Area = (N / C) × m² = N m² / C (also equivalent to Volt·meter).

questions.question: If the radius of a Gaussian sphere enclosing a point charge is doubled, the total electric flux:
questions.explanation: By Gauss's Law, Φ = Q_enclosed / ε₀. Total flux depends solely on the enclosed charge, not the surface radius.

12.title: Current Electricity
12.summary: High probability: Drift velocity (I = n·e·A·v_d), temperature coefficient of resistance, Kirchhoff's Junction & Loop rules, and Wheatstone bridge balance condition.

questions.question: Two resistors of 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal 6V battery. Total current drawn is:
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: R_eq = (3 × 6)/(3 + 6) = 2 Ω. Current I = V / R_eq = 6V / 2Ω = 3 A.
